correctness.rationale: For every finite rook graph, selected edge sets are exactly disjoint induced \(K_2\) and induced \(P_3\) blocks. The proof establishes this in both directions, identifies labeled (1,2),(2,1),(2,2) resource shapes with multiplicities 1,1,4, and rigorously applies the two-sort exponential formula. The triple factorial coefficient extraction and distinguished-row recurrence follow independently. Resource counts prove the maximum and odd-square parity obstruction and explicit constructions attain all cases. The standalone direct checker passed 328221 exhaustive candidate edge subsets, 217579 bounded-degree candidates on two larger boards and independent recurrence/formula checks for 225 parameter pairs; finite tests are not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The EOP definition and general induced-star decomposition are prior art (2022); product bounds and complexity (2024), injective edge-coloring numbers (2023), and generic EOP parameter-value characterization (2025) do not imply the claimed full polynomial on complete-by-complete Cartesian products. Claims were compared as logical implications, including labeled-part block counts, not titles; possible older induced-star enumerations remain a documented residual risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed or differently named enumeration of induced disjoint stars in line graphs of complete bipartite graphs might be equivalent; targeted search is not a universal novelty certificate.
The 2025 work supplies further general value characterizations but no inspected rook-counting identity; future discoveries could change attribution.

value.rationale: The closed two-parameter edge-open-packing polynomial and explicit recursion determine every exact cardinality, not just a maximum, for a classical family; it also yields the sharp odd-square loss from \(\min\{m,n\}\), a nontrivial parity boundary. This quantifies admissible edge-color classes for injective edge coloring, though not their partitions. The full family is mathematically motivated by Cartesian-product EOP literature and not an arbitrary numerical slice.
